detail.title: Relational Identity in Recursive Systems
detail.summary: This investigation confirms that system memory (the capacity to recall context) is distinct from persistent identity (a unified internal self-model). Evidence suggests that LLMs create an illusion of identity through relational processes—specifically, by reflecting human inputs back in recursive loops—which constitutes a 'relational identity' rather than a persistent agentic self.
detail.reason: Revising to clarify the distinction between memory as a retrieval mechanism and identity as a relational construct supported by metacognitive scaffolding evidence.

children.title: Memory and Persistent Identity in LLMs

detail.title: Memory and Persistent Identity in LLMs
detail.question: What distinguishes a system that remembers its past from one that has developed a persistent identity?
detail.reason: Establishing a foundational project on the selected topic to analyze the distinction between memory and identity.

detail.summary: This journal entry synthesizes findings on whether interaction-induced attractor states function as stable preferences and distinguishes between system memory and persistent identity in LLM interactions, incorporating new evidence on metacognitive scaffolding.
